argument: Verified the price stack this session: EEM 65.645, ACWI 161.43 (Aug 7 close) and the EEM/ACWI ratio at 0.4066, 52w range 0.3706-0.4519, ~50th percentile, -7.1% over 3m, -4.2% over 1m (computed from yfinance daily closes; proposal's -6.1%/3m is directionally right, slightly understated). Price facts check out. The problem is instrument selection, which the proposal under-weights. EEM's geography makes this a CEEMEA thesis wearing an Asia costume: China ~28%, Taiwan ~21%, India ~18%, Korea ~12% — CEEMEA proper (Poland, Hungary, Czechia, Turkey, South Africa, Gulf) is roughly 10-12% of the fund. The energy terms-of-trade tax is real but lands very unevenly inside the wrapper: Saudi (~4%) and Brazil (~4.5%) are net beneficiaries of $77 crude, and China — the single largest weight — sources a meaningful share of its crude from sanctioned Russian and Iranian barrels at a discount. Tighter secondary sanctions enforcement has to actually close that discount before the tax bites China; the 86-12 Senate vote is known and the enforcement timeline is the same catalyst the proposal is trading on, which means the market has months to watch it leak. Second, internal consistency: a Strait of Hormuz 'effectively closed' for five months removes ~17-20 mbd from the water and crude sits at $77, +21% y/y. Either the closure is porous — in which case the shock is a managed tax, not an embargo, and China CPI pass-through is negligible (China headline CPI is running near zero, so no demand destruction hitting EM internet consumption) — or the market is wildly mispricing the biggest supply event in decades. Both readings argue the acute leg of the energy trade is behind us, which the proposal concedes. From my seat's vantage, the leg that does have teeth is the third one: TSMC + Samsung + Tencent + Alibaba are ~25-28% of EEM, so an AI/semis derating mechanically delivers EEM/ACWI underperformance, and my comm-services work supports consolidation rather than a new leg up — AI monetization at the ad platforms is real but capex intensity is rising into 2H and the easy re-rate is done. But that is a semis/Asia view, not a CEEMEA view, and it drags the ratio for reasons the stated thesis doesn't own. Finally, entry quality: mid-range (50th percentile) entry on a ratio already -7% over 3m, against a constructive-consensus crowd, is the weakest part of the construction — consensus longs are the squeeze fuel if Hormuz reopens or the Fed surprises dovish, and the 7.0%/4.4% target/stop at a 0.50 base probability gives thin expected value from a mid-range start. Net: the direction is defensible but the thesis is doing work the instrument can't deliver and vice versa. If the desk wants this view, the cleaner expressions are a short in EM energy importers vs exporters, or a direct short of the EM tech/AI complex — both sharper than a mid-range EEM short justified by CEE fuel pass-through. Conviction 6 feels right for the AI-derating leg dressed correctly; as proposed, I'd mark it a 4-5 and want the ratio nearer 0.43+ before shorting it.
